2. Brief facts of the case are that on 14.12.2022 at about 06:15 PM, Sh. Vikram Singh (since deceased) was riding a scooty bearing no.UP-16CD-5471 towards Dadri.

When he reached in front of Daksh Medical store, Village Tilpata, PS Surajpur Gautambudh Nagar, U.P. , he was hit by a speeding Canter bearing no. HR-55W-1909 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) from behind.

Due to the impact, victim sustained grievous injuries and was rushed to Naveen Hospital,
Greater Noida.
He was referred and later shifted to Kailash Hospital, Greater Noida where he succumbed to the injuries and Misc DJ No. 226/23 Neetu Singh & ors vs. Surender Singh & ors.

U.P. Police investigated the matter and filed a chargesheet before concerned Criminal Court while the present claim petition was filed before this Tribunal.
4. As per record, the offending vehicle was driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3.
Written statement /reply was filed by all the respondents denying their liability to compensate the petitioners.

5. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 30.04.2024.
1) Whether the deceased suffered fatal injuries in a road traffic accident on 14.12.2022 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR-55W-1909 being driven by R1, owned by R-2 and insured with R3?

OPP. 
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom ?

OPP. 
3) Relief.
6.
Before any evidence could be led in this matter, a legal offer was filed on behalf of the insurance company.

The said legal offer was acceptable to the petitioner to the extent of the principle compensation amount, however parties remained at disagreement regarding the payment of interest, the rate of which interest, if any, be directed to be paid and the period from which such interest would be determined.

8.
As regards, respondent no.3/insurance company has admitted its liability to compensate the petitioners.
The quantum of principle compensation has been agreed by both the parties for a sum of Rs.49,41,770/-.This Tribunal
finds the offer to be just and reasonable.
The only issue requiring adjudication, thus, whether any interest payable by the insurance company, if so, to what extent /period and at what rate.
It is argued by ld. Counsel for petitioner that the interest be paid by the insurance company from the date of filing of the petition till realization of the principle amount.

On the other hand, it is argued on behalf of insurance company that mere filing of the claim petition is no ground to claim interest for the entire period during which the petitioner did not even file or supply complete criminal record to enable the insurance company to file a reply.
Perusal of the record reveals that though the claim petition was filed on 18.01.2023, copy of the chargesheet was filed later on 09.05.2023.
Even after two successive dates, insurance company did not file any reply.
Written statement was filed by the respondents on 13.04.2024.
It is pertinent to note that as per Misc DJ No. 226/23 Neetu Singh & ors vs. Surender Singh & ors.

2025.05.05 16:32:34 +0530 the record, non supply of the copy of the chargesheet or the criminal record did not prevent the insurance company from filing the written statement.
As such, same cannot be a ground for declining the interest of the petitioner for such period.
Record further does not reveal any adverse conduct on the part of the petitioner such as not having diligently pursued their claim, disentitling them from claiming interest.

On the other hand, the fact that the insurance company has come up with an offer to settle, only after matter was proceeded for evidence,
renders the insurance company liable to pay simple interest @7.5 p.a. on the principle agreed amount, from the date of filing of petition till actual realization.
